justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Pre-habilitation and post-transplant rehab reduce complications, ICU time, and improve functional recovery.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Specialized fellowship or institutional training; limited formal certification pathways.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable exclusively at solid organ transplant centers; not relevant outside this narrow setting.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Covered under standard PT/OT codes in transplant centers; no certification-specific billing premium.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Demand limited to transplant centers; valued by UNOS-affiliated programs.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Transplant patients highly motivated; functional recovery goal is personally meaningful.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Transplant patients are deeply embedded in insurance/hospital systems; essentially zero direct cash-pay market exists for this population.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Even where rare, the payer mix is institutional and reimbursement-bound, with no consumer brand recognition to command premium pricing.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Genuinely rare niche, but rarity does not translate to private-practice differentiation since the patient population doesn't seek outpatient cash services.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Not a scalable practice model; clinical care happens inside transplant centers, not standalone clinics with employed clinicians.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Public has near-zero awareness of transplant rehab as a discrete service to seek out.
justifications.business.efficiency: Typically a CEU-based pathway rather than a multi-year credential, so reasonably efficient to obtain, but ROI is poor outside acute care.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Not a board specialty or ABPTRFE-recognized credential; viewed as a niche clinical interest rather than promotion-grade.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Modest but growing literature base; faculty in acute care can publish case series and program-development papers.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Fits narrowly into acute care or medical/surgical electives; limited core curricular utility.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Evidence base is largely observational/cohort with few RCTs; growing but still thin compared to mainstream rehab topics.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely listed as preferred in faculty postings; more relevant for clinical residency directors in acute care.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Lower time burden than a residency or board cert, so reasonable on a cost-per-credential basis.
